mainTopic: Which animals and grains may be tithed together for מעשר, and how far apart flocks can be and still join for מעשר בהמה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a challenge: why can't בקר and צאן be tithed one for the other? אביי answers from the word העשירי that each group gives its own tenth. Sheep and goats, though, are tithed together, because the one word צאן makes them a single group. The גמרא then asks why the word דגן does not likewise make all grains one group. אביי answers from the plural ראשיתם. רבא answers that the words בקר וצאן are extra, because חיה is already excluded by the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת and the separation of species comes from a קל וחומר. The word דגן, by contrast, is needed to exclude other crops. After a challenge from רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן and a second version of רבא's answer based on a היקש to מעשר דגן, the גמרא resolves an apparent contradiction in רבא's statements in two ways. Then a new משנה teaches that flocks join for מעשר בהמה within 16 מיל, that a middle flock can link flocks up to 32 מיל apart, and that according to רבי מאיר the ירדן divides them. The גמרא brings a source from ירמיהו and explains why the משנה mentions 32 מיל. It ends with רב and שמואל disputing how many animals the middle flock needs.

steps.title: Challenge: let cattle and flock be tithed together
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a challenge raised on the previous amud: בקר and צאן should be tithed one for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them be tithed from one for the other!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a challenge that began on the previous amud. Someone argues that cattle and sheep should be allowed to count together for מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger thinks there is no reason to keep בקר and צאן apart, so one tenth could cover both. This goes against the rule that each group must be tithed on its own. The next step answers him from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: from one for the other (one group covering the other)
the tithe of animals, where every tenth animal is holy

phrases.english: Let them be tithed from one for the other!
phrases.notes: End of a challenge that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that בקר and צאן are not tithed one for the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The challenger sees no reason to separate them, so they should combine for the tithe.

steps.title: The word העשירי means each group gives its own tenth
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the word העשירי that the tithe is given separately from each group.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the verse says 'the tenth.' Give a tenth for this one, and give a tenth for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a word in the פסוק. The word העשירי teaches that each group gives its own tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions בקר and צאן and then says 'the tenth.' אביי reads this as a tenth for each group listed. So the cattle get their own count and the sheep get their own count.

phrases.english: He said to him: The verse says, 'the tenth,'
give a tenth for this one (the herd)
and give a tenth for that one (the flock).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בקר and צאן could combine into one tithe.
steps.terutzMaskana: העשירי requires a separate tenth from each group.

steps.title: Then sheep and goats should also be separate
steps.stepSummary: If each kind needs its own tenth, sheep and goats should also be tithed separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, sheep and goats too should be tithed separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's answer. If species are separated, why are sheep and goats not separated as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sheep and goats are two different species, just as cattle differ from sheep. If העשירי means a tenth for each kind, it seems sheep and goats should each need their own count too. Yet the הלכה is that they combine.

phrases.english: If so, sheep and goats too (should be tithed separately)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of העשירי as a tenth for each kind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reading applies to every kind, it should also split sheep from goats, which is not the הלכה.

steps.title: The word צאן makes all sheep and goats one group
steps.stepSummary: The single word צאן teaches that sheep and goats together count as one flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or the flock' means all flock animals are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah used one word, צאן, for both sheep and goats. That makes them one group for the tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah splits animals into two groups only: בקר and צאן. Sheep and goats both fall under the one word צאן, so they are tithed together. The separation from step 2 applies only between the two groups the verse names.

phrases.english: 'Or the flock' means that all flock animals are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a single collective word as one category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sheep and goats would need separate tithing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sheep and goats are one צאן and are tithed together.
steps.whatToRemember: בקר and צאן are tithed separately because of העשירי. Sheep and goats are tithed together because they are one צאן.

steps.title: Then all grain should be one group too
steps.stepSummary: By the same logic, the word דגן should make all kinds of grain one group for תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let us say that 'grain' means all grain is one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the צאן reasoning to produce. If one word joins sheep and goats, the one word דגן should join all grains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה is that you cannot separate תרומה from one kind of grain to cover another kind, such as wheat for barley. The צאן logic seems to argue the opposite, since the verse says just 'דגן.' So the challenge is: why are grains different?

phrases.english: Here too, let us say
that 'grain' means all grain is one!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי לֵימָא מַשְׁמַע כׇּל דָּגָן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in step 4 to challenge the rule for grain.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that different kinds of grain cannot be tithed one for the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one collective word unites sheep and goats, the one word דגן should unite all grains.

steps.title: אביי: the plural ראשיתם separates the grains
steps.stepSummary: אביי, supported by רבי אילעא, answers that the plural ראשיתם requires a separate first portion from each kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Their first part.' And רבי אילעא also said: 'Their first part.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the grain verse says ראשיתם, 'their first part,' in the plural. רבי אילעא gives the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural form means each kind of grain has its own 'first part' that must be given. This extra word cancels the idea that דגן makes all grain one group. There is no such plural word for צאן.

phrases.english: Abaye said: 'Their first part,'
and likewise Rabbi Ile'a said: 'Their first part.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A plural word in the verse breaks the unity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All grains are one דגן and could be tithed together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of ראשיתם, each kind of grain needs its own תרומה.

steps.title: רבא: even without ראשיתם, grain is not one group
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even without the word ראשיתם, one cannot read דגן as uniting all grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without 'their first part,' you cannot say that 'grain' means all grain is one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same challenge. He says the challenge never works, even without ראשיתם. His explanation begins in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי needed an extra word to separate the grains. רבא argues that the word דגן never meant 'one group' in the first place. He will show that the צאן reading had a special basis that does not exist for דגן.

phrases.english: Rava said: Even without 'their first part,'
that 'grain' means all grain is one
you cannot say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 5, different from אביי's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the word ראשיתם stops דגן from uniting all grains.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word דגן never implied that all grains are one group.

steps.title: Why the word צאן really does unite sheep and goats
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that צאן teaches unity because the Torah could have simply written 'all animal tithe.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, there we say 'or the flock' means all flock animals are one. For if you thought sheep and goats were also separate, let the verse write 'and all the animal tithe.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the word צאן teaches that sheep and goats are one group. The Torah named בקר and צאן even though it could have used one general phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every species needed its own tenth, the Torah could have just written 'וכל מעשר בהמה.' The rule that species are not tithed for one another would then come from a קל וחומר, which step 11 lays out. Naming the two groups shows the split is only between בקר and צאן, with צאן as one unit. רבא is setting up a contrast with דגן, which he finishes in step 12.

phrases.english: Granted, there we say:
'or the flock' means all flock animals are one,
for if it entered your mind
that sheep and goats too (are separate),
let it write 'and all the animal tithe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבא's explanation for his claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the word צאן truly teaches that sheep and goats are one group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah named בקר and צאן instead of writing the general phrase 'וכל מעשר בהמה.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's צאן reading rests on the Torah's choice of words. He will argue that the word דגן has no such basis.

steps.title: Objection: the general phrase would include wild animals
steps.stepSummary: An expected objection: had the Torah written 'all animal tithe,' one might include חיה, so the words בקר and צאן were needed to exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: had it written 'all the animal tithe,' I would have thought even wild animals are included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a possible objection to his own proof. Perhaps the Torah named בקר and צאן only to exclude wild animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If naming בקר and צאן was needed to exclude חיה, then those words are not extra. They would teach nothing about sheep and goats being one group, and רבא's proof would fall apart.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי כְּתִיב ״כׇּל מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה״,
phrases.english: And if you would say: if it had written 'all the animal tithe,'
I would have thought even a wild animal (is included)

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי כְּתִיב ״כׇּל מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible objection to the proof in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the words בקר and צאן were not needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The specific words may have been needed to exclude חיה, so they would not be free to teach anything else.

steps.title: Wild animals are already excluded by תחת תחת
steps.stepSummary: חיה is already excluded by the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת from קדשים, so the words בקר and צאן were not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'under' and 'under' from sacrificial animals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection. Wild animals are already excluded through a גזירה שוה, so the Torah did not need specific words to exclude them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תחת appears both for קדשים ('seven days under its mother') and for מעשר בהמה ('passes under the rod'). Since a חיה cannot be brought as a קרבן, it is also not subject to מעשר בהמה. That leaves the words בקר and צאן free, so רבא's proof from step 8 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: under; the shared word for the גזירה שוה
a law learned from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the words בקר and צאן are not needed to exclude חיה, which תחת תחת already excludes. So they teach that sheep and goats are one group. רבא's contrast with grain continues next.
steps.confusionAlert: The two תחת verses are different. One is 'under its mother' (קדשים, ויקרא 22:27). The other is 'under the rod' (מעשר, ויקרא 27:32). The shared word is what links the two topics.

phrases.english: He derives 'under' and 'under' from sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 9 and restores the proof in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the exclusion comes from another source (a גזירה שוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words בקר and צאן were needed to exclude חיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חיה is excluded by תחת תחת, so the words are free to teach that צאן is one group.

steps.title: The extra words בקר וצאן teach that sheep and goats are one kind
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that a קל וחומר from new and old grain would already forbid tithing one species for another. So the words בקר וצאן must be there to teach that sheep and goats, both called צאן, can be tithed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: We could already learn, through a קל וחומר from new and old grain, that one species is not tithed for another. So why do I need the words 'cattle and flock'? To teach that cattle and flock are not tithed one for the other, but sheep and goats are tithed together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof from step 8. Since the words בקר וצאן are not needed for anything else, he shows what new lesson they must teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed that חיה is already excluded, so the Torah could simply have written 'all animal tithe.' The rule that different species are not tithed together could then come from a קל וחומר: if new and old grain, which are not כלאים, cannot be tithed for each other, then different animal species, which are כלאים, certainly cannot. The words בקר וצאן are therefore extra, and they teach that sheep and goats, both included in צאן, count as one kind for tithing.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
This year's grain and last year's grain
Tithed from one group on behalf of the other

phrases.english: and it would come through a kal vachomer from new and old grain;
phrases.notes: New and old grain aren't כלאים, yet they can't be tithed for each other. So different animal species surely can't be.

phrases.english: so why do I need 'cattle and flock'?

phrases.aramaic: בָּקָר וָצֹאן הוּא דְּאֵין מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: It is cattle and flock that are not tithed one for the other,
but sheep and goats are tithed together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 10. Now that חיה is excluded another way, רבא can show that בקר וצאן are extra words that teach a new lesson.
steps.raayaObject: Sheep and goats count as one kind for מעשר בהמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words בקר וצאן, which are not needed once the קל וחומר from חדש וישן exists
steps.whatToRemember: The words בקר וצאן are 'extra,' so they teach that sheep and goats count as one kind for tithing.

steps.title: The word דגן is needed to exclude other crops
steps.stepSummary: רבא contrasts grain with animals. The word דגן is not extra, because it is needed to exclude other kinds of produce from Torah-level tithes. So it cannot teach that all grains are one kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with grain, could the Torah have managed without writing 'grain'? No. It is needed to exclude other kinds of produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes his distinction. Unlike בקר וצאן, the word דגן has a necessary job of its own, so no extra lesson about uniting grains can be drawn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning a new lesson from a word works only when the word is not needed for anything else. The word דגן is needed to limit Torah-level tithes to grain and leave out other crops. Since it is already 'used up,' it cannot also teach that wheat and barley may be tithed together.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it be enough? Could it manage?

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִי סַגִּיא דְּלָא כְּתִיב ״דָּגָן״?
phrases.english: But here, could it manage without the word 'grain' written?
It is needed to exclude other kinds of produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא מִי סַגִּיא דְּלָא כְּתִיב דָּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 11. בקר וצאן are extra words, but דגן is needed for its own job.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: צאן teaches that sheep and goats are one kind because the word is extra. דגן teaches no such unity, because it is needed to exclude other crops.
steps.whatToRemember: A word can teach a new lesson only if it is not already needed for something else. That is the difference between צאן and דגן.

steps.title: Perhaps cattle and sheep should be mixed together
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן challenges רבא. Maybe the words בקר וצאן teach the opposite: that cattle and sheep should be combined and tithed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן objected: Say instead that the verse means to mix the cattle in with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רבא's reading of the words בקר וצאן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read the words as keeping cattle and sheep separate. רב הונא argues that listing them together in one phrase could just as easily mean they are joined into one tithing group. If so, the separation would need a different source.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman objected to this:
Say it means to mix cattle with the flock!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading of בקר וצאן from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that בקר וצאן teaches that cattle and sheep are not tithed for each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining the two words in one phrase could mean they are combined, not kept apart.

steps.title: רבא also learns the separation from העשירי
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן answers that רבא accepts אביי's source, the word העשירי. That word already teaches that cattle and sheep are tithed separately, so mixing them is not an option.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן said to him: רבא also holds of the word 'the tenth.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers רב הונא's challenge by pointing to another verse that רבא accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word העשירי, which אביי uses, already shows that cattle and sheep are separate tithing groups. Since the separation is settled, the reading that mixes them is ruled out. The words בקר וצאן therefore stay free to teach that sheep and goats are one kind.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds of it, he accepts it
'The tenth' (from the verse on animal tithe)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman said to him:
As for Rava, he also holds of 'the tenth.'
phrases.notes: Meaning: רבא also accepts אביי's lesson from העשירי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a second source that רבא also accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בקר וצאן might teach that cattle and sheep are mixed
steps.terutzMaskana: העשירי already separates cattle and sheep, so the mixing reading is ruled out

steps.title: A second version: a היקש to grain tithe keeps cattle and sheep apart
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבא says that even without העשירי, cattle and sheep cannot be tithed together. מעשר בהמה is compared to מעשר דגן, and just as grain is not tithed from one type for another, animals are not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: Even without 'the tenth,' you cannot say cattle and flock are tithed for each other. Animal tithe is compared to grain tithe. Just as grain tithe is not taken from one type for a different type, so too animal tithe is not taken from one type for a different type.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of רבא's answer. Here he uses a different source to show that cattle and sheep are never combined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבא does not need העשירי at all. Because the Torah links מעשר בהמה with מעשר דגן, the grain rule carries over: different types are not tithed for each other. That rule alone rules out רב הונא's idea of mixing cattle with sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared through a היקש (a link the Torah makes between two laws)
From one type on behalf of a different type

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 12. There, דגן could not teach that grains are one kind. Here, the link to grain teaches separation: different types are kept apart.

phrases.english: Some say Rava said:
Even without 'the tenth' you could not say

phrases.aramaic: בָּקָר וָצֹאן מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: that cattle and flock are tithed one for the other,
because animal tithe is compared to grain tithe:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ לָא,
phrases.english: just as grain tithe is not taken from one type for a different type,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ לָא.
phrases.english: so too animal tithe is not taken from one type for a different type.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אָמַר רָבָא בְּלֹא עֲשִׂירִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the challenge of step 13, replacing מר זוטרא's answer from העשירי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learns the separation from a היקש instead of from העשירי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without העשירי, cattle and sheep might be mixed together
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש to מעשר דגן forbids tithing one type for another, so cattle and sheep stay separate
steps.whyThisMatters: Both versions agree that cattle and sheep are never tithed together. They disagree only about the source for that rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Cattle and sheep are separate for tithing, while sheep and goats count as one kind. The separation comes from either העשירי or the היקש to grain.

steps.title: רבא seems to contradict himself about the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא himself limited the היקש between grain and animal tithes to the 'year' rule only. So how can he use it to forbid tithing one species for another?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רבא who said: 'Year by year' – I compared them only regarding the year, and not regarding any other matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבא's answer from step 15 by quoting another statement of רבא that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבא compared מעשר בהמה to מעשר דגן to teach that you cannot tithe one type for another. But elsewhere רבא said the words 'שנה שנה' link the two tithes only for one rule: you cannot tithe this year's animals or produce with last year's. If the היקש is limited to the year rule, it cannot also forbid mixing species.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (opens a contradiction)
'Year by year' – the פסוק that links the two tithes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge from a ברייתא or a פסוק. It is רבא against רבא: two statements of the same אמורא that seem to clash.

phrases.english: But isn't it Rava who said:
"Year" – regarding the year I compared them,
phrases.notes: The words 'שנה שנה' link animal tithe to grain tithe.

phrases.english: and not regarding any other matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רבא's answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of the היקש between מעשר בהמה and מעשר דגן to forbid tithing one species for another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself limited that היקש to the year rule only, so it cannot teach anything about species.

steps.title: רבא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: First answer: רבא retracted his earlier statement that limited the היקש to the year rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא retracted from that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction simply: רבא changed his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's later view is that the היקש covers more than the year rule. It also forbids tithing one type of animal for another. So there is no real contradiction; one statement replaced the other.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; he changed his mind

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction – one statement was given up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds both views at the same time, and they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא abandoned the 'year only' limitation. He now applies the היקש to species as well.

steps.title: One of the statements was really said by רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: one of the two clashing statements was actually said by רב פפא, not רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: one of them was said by רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative answer to the same contradiction: the two statements come from two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, רבא never contradicted himself. One view belongs to רבא and the other to רב פפא, who was רבא's close student. That is why their statements were sometimes mixed up. Two different אמוראים may disagree, so the problem disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction in רבא's statements is solved in two ways: either רבא retracted, or one of the statements belongs to רב פפא.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
one of them
phrases.notes: Some versions say מיניה (of it), in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is מינייהי (of them).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution – the statements belong to two different אמוראים
steps.terutzMaskana: One statement was said by רב פפא, so there is no self-contradiction.

steps.title: Flocks join for animal tithe within sixteen mil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that flocks combine for מעשר בהמה if they are within 16 מיל of each other. Two flocks 32 מיל apart do not combine, but a flock in the middle can link them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Animals combine for animal tithe within the walking range of a grazing animal. How far is that range? Sixteen מיל. If two flocks were 32 מיל apart, they do not combine. If he also had animals in the middle, he brings them all to the middle and tithes them there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the maximum distance between flocks that still count as one group for מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flocks up to 16 מיל apart count as one group, so every tenth animal is taken from the combined count. At 32 מיל apart, the two flocks are too far to join. But a middle flock is within 16 מיל of each side, so it connects them. The owner gathers all of them in the middle and tithes them together.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together; combines into one count
The full walking range of a grazing animal

steps.confusionAlert: The 32-מיל case is not a new limit. It simply means each outer flock is 16 מיל from the middle, but 32 מיל from the other outer flock, which is too far to join directly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines what counts as 'one flock' for מעשר בהמה. That decides which animals go into the count of ten.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Animal tithe combines
within the full walking range of a grazing animal,
And how much is the walking range of a grazing animal?
Sixteen mil.
If there were between these and those
thirty-two mil – they do not combine.
If he had animals in the middle –
he brings them and tithes them in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מִצְטָרֵף כִּמְלֹא רֶגֶל בְּהֵמָה רוֹעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: distance between flocks
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flocks within 16 מיל combine for מעשר בהמה. Flocks 32 מיל apart do not, unless a middle flock links them and all are tithed in the middle.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the Jordan River separates flocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר adds that the ירדן divides flocks for מעשר בהמה, even if they are close together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The ירדן divides with regard to animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the opinion of רבי מאיר: a river boundary, the ירדן, splits flocks into separate groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, only distance matters (16 מיל). רבי מאיר adds a physical boundary. Animals on opposite sides of the ירדן never combine, even if they are well within 16 מיל of each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The Jordan divides with regard to animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an additional limit to the distance rule of step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the ירדן separates flocks for מעשר בהמה regardless of distance.

steps.title: What is the source for the sixteen-mil rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's distance rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that flocks combine within the range of a grazing animal. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a rule and a number but gave no reason. The גמרא wants both a פסוק that flocks combine based on one shepherd's range, and a basis for the specific number 16.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (opens the discussion of the משנה)
From where are these things derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Scriptural source and basis for combining flocks within 16 מיל

steps.title: A verse about one counter and the shepherd's sixteen-mil view
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא cites ירמיהו: 'the flock shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts.' The חכמים also have a tradition that a shepherd's eye controls up to 16 מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: The פסוק says, 'The flock shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts them.' And the חכמים know that a shepherd's eye controls up to sixteen מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers the question with a פסוק plus a known tradition about how far a shepherd can watch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that a 'flock' means animals under one counter, one shepherd. The tradition supplies the number: a shepherd can oversee up to 16 מיל. So animals within that range count as one flock for מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים have an accepted tradition
The eye controls it; can watch over it

steps.whatToRemember: The 16-מיל rule has two parts. The פסוק teaches that a flock is defined by one shepherd who counts it. The חכמים' tradition says a shepherd can oversee up to 16 מיל.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
For the verse states:
"Again the flock shall pass
under the hands of the one who counts,"
and the Sages have an established tradition
that up to sixteen mil
the eye of the shepherd controls it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ירמיהו defines a flock as animals under one counter. The tradition sets a shepherd's range at 16 מיל.

steps.title: Does the 32 מיל line contradict the 16 מיל rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 32 מיל line. It infers that flocks under 32 מיל would combine, which contradicts the earlier rule of only 16 מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the flocks were 32 מיל apart, they do not combine. That implies only 32 is too far, so less than that does combine. But the משנה already taught 16 מיל, meaning no more than that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and reads an implication into it. It then shows that this implication clashes with the משנה's own earlier rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 32 מיל is the point where flocks stop combining, then 20 or 30 מיל should still combine. But the משנה's basic rule says flocks combine only within 16 מיל. So the 32 number seems to contradict the 16 number.

keyTerms.meaning: they combine (join together into one group)
a unit of distance, roughly a kilometer
but it teaches (introduces a contradiction from the text)

steps.confusionAlert: There are not two different distance rules here. The 16 מיל rule is the real limit, and the גמרא is only asking why the משנה mentions 32 at all.

phrases.english: If there were between these and those
thirty-two mil
they do not combine, etc.
It is only at thirty-two that they do not combine,
implying that at less than this they do combine?
But it teaches: sixteen mil,
meaning no more than that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה text after the source derivation in step 22. It reads the next clause of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that flocks 32 מיל apart do not combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its implied meaning, that anything under 32 combines, contradicts the stated 16 מיל limit.

steps.title: 32 is mentioned only to set up the middle-flock case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions 32 מיל only because its next clause teaches about a flock in the middle linking the two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 32 only because it wanted to teach the next part: if he had animals in the middle, he brings them all and tithes them in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number 32 does not set a new distance limit. It is there only to set up the next case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A middle flock can reach no more than 16 מיל to each side. So 32 מיל is the farthest apart two outer flocks can be and still be linked through a middle flock. The משנה uses 32 to describe this linking case. It does not mean that two flocks less than 32 מיל apart combine without a middle flock.

keyTerms.meaning: the later clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Because it wants to teach the latter clause:
if he had animals in the middle,
he brings them and tithes them in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The number serves to set up the next clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 32 מיל is the real limit, so anything under it combines.
steps.terutzMaskana: 16 מיל is the only limit. The 32 figure describes two flocks linked by a middle flock.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic limit is 16 מיל. Two flocks 32 מיל apart combine only through a flock in the middle.

steps.title: How many animals are needed to link the flocks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many animals must be in each flock, especially the middle one, for all three to be tithed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many animals are needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question about the middle-flock case. It is setting up the dispute between רב and שמואל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the middle flock links the two sides, the next question is about size. Does the middle flock need to be large, or does any animal there count?

phrases.english: And how many?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the middle-flock case explained in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of animals on each side and in the middle for the flocks to combine.

steps.title: רב requires five in each group
steps.stepSummary: רב says there must be five on each side and five in the middle. That way the middle five can make ten with either side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: five from here, five from there, and five in the middle. These middle five can join with this side and can join with that side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. The middle group needs five animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה applies only to a group of ten. Five in the middle plus five on either side makes ten, so the middle flock truly joins each side. Because each side forms a real group with the middle, all three count as one flock.

keyTerms.meaning: fit to join with this side

phrases.english: Rav says:
five from here and five from there
and five in the middle,
because these five
are fit to join here and fit to join there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five on each side and five in the middle, so the middle can complete ten with either side.

steps.title: שמואל says even one in the middle is enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says even one animal in the middle links the two sides. The shepherd is pictured as standing in the middle, counting everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: even five from here, five from there, and one in the middle. We view the shepherd as if he stands here in the middle, and we call him 'the one who counts.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says a single animal in the middle is enough to link the two flocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the middle animal does not need to make ten with either side. Its only job is to put the shepherd in the middle. From there he can see and count both sides, which fits the פסוק 'the one who counts' (מונה) from step 22. So the link depends on the shepherd's view, not on the number of animals.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who counts (word from the פסוק in ירמיהו)

steps.whyThisMatters: The dispute shows two ways of understanding what makes flocks one group. רב looks at the animals forming a group of ten. שמואל looks at the shepherd's ability to oversee them all.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the middle flock needs five, enough to make ten with each side. שמואל: one is enough, because the shepherd in the middle counts both sides.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
even five from here and five from there
and one in the middle,
we view the shepherd
as one who stands here in the middle,
and we apply to him the word 'one who counts.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in step 26 and gives a more lenient minimum.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even one animal in the middle suffices, since the shepherd standing there counts both sides.
